h-bar.name: Reduced Planck Constant
h-bar.description: The fundamental quantum of action (h / 2π), representing the scale at which quantum effects become dominant.

h.name: Planck Constant
h.description: The exact SI defining constant relating the energy of a photon to its electromagnetic frequency.

c.name: Speed of Light in Vacuum
c.description: The exact maximum speed at which massless particles and causal information propagate through vacuum.

G.name: Gravitational Constant
G.description: The empirical coupling constant governing gravitational attraction in Newtonian gravity and Einstein's field equations.

k-B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k-B.description: The exact SI defining constant linking average microscopic thermal energy to absolute thermodynamic temperature.

e.name: Elementary Charge
e.description: The exact magnitude of electric charge carried by a single proton or, with opposite sign, a single electron.

N-A.name: Avogadro Constant
N-A.description: The exact number of constituent particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) contained in one mole of a substance.

R.name: Molar Gas Constant
R.description: The molar equivalent of the Boltzmann constant (N_A k_B), appearing in the ideal gas law and chemical thermodynamics.

epsilon-0.name: Vacuum Electric Permittivity
epsilon-0.description: The electric polarizability of classical vacuum, linking electric displacement fields to electric fields in Maxwell's equations.

mu-0.name: Vacuum Magnetic Permeability
mu-0.description: The magnetic permeability of classical vacuum, governing the strength of magnetic fields generated by electric currents.

alpha.name: Fine-Structure Constant
alpha.description: The dimensionless coupling constant characterizing the strength of the electromagnetic interaction between elementary charged particles.

sigma-sb.name: Stefan-Boltzmann Constant
sigma-sb.description: The proportionality constant relating the total radiative power per unit area of a black body to the fourth power of its temperature.

m-e.name: Electron Mass
m-e.description: The rest mass of a stationary electron, setting the fundamental mass scale of atomic and molecular physics.

m-p.name: Proton Mass
m-p.description: The rest mass of a stationary proton, predominantly generated by quantum chromodynamic binding energy.

m-n.name: Neutron Mass
m-n.description: The rest mass of a free neutron, exceeding the proton mass by roughly 1.293 MeV/c² and enabling beta decay.

u.name: Atomic Mass Constant
u.description: One-twelfth the rest mass of an unbound neutral carbon-12 atom in its nuclear and electronic ground state (1 Da).

R-inf.name: Rydberg Constant
R-inf.description: The limiting wavenumber of the highest-energy photon emitted by a hydrogen atom with an infinitely massive nucleus.

a-0.name: Bohr Radius
a-0.description: The characteristic spatial scale of the hydrogen atom, equal to the most probable ground-state electron-nucleus distance.

mu-B.name: Bohr Magneton
mu-B.description: The natural unit of electronic magnetic dipole moment (eℏ / 2m_e) arising from orbital or spin angular momentum.

mu-N.name: Nuclear Magneton
mu-N.description: The natural unit of nuclear magnetic dipole moment (eℏ / 2m_p) used in nuclear physics and NMR spectroscopy.

F.name: Faraday Constant
F.description: The exact electric charge carried by one mole of elementary charges (N_A e), foundational to electrochemistry.

l-P.name: Planck Length
l-P.description: The natural length scale √(ℏG/c³) at which quantum mechanical and general relativistic spacetime effects converge.

t-P.name: Planck Time
t-P.description: The time required for light in vacuum to traverse one Planck length, √(ℏG/c⁵).

m-P.name: Planck Mass
m-P.description: The natural mass scale √(ℏc/G) where a particle's Compton wavelength matches its Schwarzschild radius.
